title: Trapping Rain Water — Two Elements
problem: Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map, compute trapped water.
intuition: Water requires at least two opposing boundaries and an intermediate dip.
invariant: When length < 3, trapped water is mathematically 0.

scenes.title: Test Case: Two Elements
scenes.narration: Testing input [3,1] (Array with length 2. Cannot form a container between two walls.). Expected output: 0.

dialogue.text: Evaluating test case 'Two Elements' with input: [3,1].
How will our two-pointer invariant handle this boundary condition?

scenes.title: Corner Case Handled: Length 2
scenes.narration: Because length is 2 < 3, no two opposing walls can trap water. Returns 0 immediately.

dialogue.text: Zero water trapped. Array length < 3: cannot form a basin.
Correct. A container requires at least two boundary walls and one interior cell.
